1use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::content::ops::{LineCap, LineJoin, Transform};
2
3pub(crate) fn convert_transform(t: Transform) -> kurbo::Affine {
4    kurbo::Affine::new([t.0.as_f64(), t.1.as_f64(), t.2.as_f64(), t.3.as_f64(), t.4.as_f64(), t.5.as_f64()])
5}
6
7pub(crate) fn convert_line_cap(lc: LineCap) -> kurbo::Cap {
8    match lc.0.as_i64() {
9        0 => kurbo::Cap::Butt,
10        1 => kurbo::Cap::Round,
11        2 => kurbo::Cap::Square,
12        _ => kurbo::Cap::Butt,
13    }
14}
15
16pub(crate) fn convert_line_join(lc: LineJoin) -> kurbo::Join {
17    match lc.0.as_i64() {
18        0 => kurbo::Join::Miter,
19        1 => kurbo::Join::Round,
20        2 => kurbo::Join::Bevel,
21        _ => kurbo::Join::Miter,
22    }
23}

25/// PdfCraft patch (61): the line width to keep for a `w` operand or an ExtGState `/LW`. ISO
26/// 32000-2 §8.4.3.2 makes 0 "the thinnest line that can be rendered at device resolution" but
27/// says nothing of a negative width; it is drawn as 0, as is one that isn't finite, so no device
28/// sees a width below zero.
29pub(crate) fn convert_line_width(width: f32) -> f32 {
30    if width.is_finite() && width > 0.0 { width } else { 0.0 }
31}
32
33/// PdfCraft patch (61): the dash array to keep for a `d` operator or an ExtGState `/D`. ISO
34/// 32000-2 §8.4.3.6 requires numbers that "shall be nonnegative and not all zero". A pattern that
35/// breaks that (all zero, a negative or a non-finite entry) is kept as `[]`, a solid line, rather
36/// than cut into dashes the zero-entry workaround below would make a hundredth of a point long.
37pub(crate) fn convert_dash_array(dashes: impl Iterator<Item = f32>) -> smallvec::SmallVec<[f32; 4]> {
38    let dashes: smallvec::SmallVec<[f32; 4]> = dashes.collect();
39    if dashes.iter().any(|d| !d.is_finite() || *d < 0.0) || dashes.iter().all(|d| *d == 0.0) {
40        return smallvec::SmallVec::new();
41    }
42    // kurbo apparently cannot properly deal with dashes that are exactly 0.
43    dashes.into_iter().map(|d| if d == 0.0 { 0.01 } else { d }).collect()
44}
